    ANDREW HINZ’S MOTION TO INTERVENE AND COMMENTS ON FEDERAL
      INTERCONNECTION TARIFFS FOR LARGE LOADS CO-LOCATED AT
                      GENERATING FACILITIES

        Any and all tariffs approved by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC)

and/or approved by an entity regulated by FERC to interconnect large loads co-located at

generating facilities must meet the following requirements to preclude violating the Natural Gas

Act and The Constitution of the United States of America:

             1. The comprehensive economic public benefit of any Large Load and any Co-

                 Located Generating Facility subject to any such tariff must be established and

                 considered and demonstrated to mutually benefit ALL ratepayers, regardless of

                 any other tariff terms and conditions.

             2. Any Large-Load Customer and any Co-Located Generating Facility must have

                 open and free access to any such tariff.

             3. States and Indigenous Tribes or Nations must have the ability to approve or reject

                 any terms of any interconnection under any such tariff.

             4. Any such tariff must include demand response conditions that preclude the Large

                 Load and/or Co-Located Generating Facility from having any negative impact on

                 congested grids during peak demand or public emergency response.


Motion to Intervene and Comments

Federal Tariffs for Large Loads Co-Located at Generating Facilities 1
         Below please find my Motion to Intervene and Comments for any proposed Federal

Interconnection Tariffs for Large Loads Co-Located at Generating Facilities. For the reasons

stated below, the Commission should grant this motion to intervene and confer party status on

Andrew Hinz and enter these comments into the official record for the named proceedings for

Interconnection Tariffs for Large Loads Co-Located at Generating Facilities.



                              I.       MOTION TO INTERVENE

        I live in the State of Maryland. The State of Maryland has begun to estimate the amount

of money taxpayers will need to invest in adaptation and mitigation to climate change caused by

burning petroleum, methane, and other fossil fuels. The estimates are staggering and my

contribution to meet the amounts estimated, under all practical taxation and revenue generation

scenarios, exceeds my ability to make that contribution and continue to live. Federal electricity

interconnection tariffs that ignore the costs I must pay to adapt to and mitigate climate change

are unjust and unreasonable. Federal electricity interconnection tariffs that subvert state law

enacted to adapt to and mitigate climate change costs are unjust and unreasonable. Federal

electricity interconnection tariffs that threaten public health during constrained grid and extreme

weather conditions and other public health emergencies are unjust and unreasonable. The costs

of climate change from consuming fossil fuels (costs to adapt to climate change, costs to mitigate

the effects of climate change, and costs to reduce further climate change) must be included in the

consideration of any and all federal tariffs providing connection of any Large Loads Co-Located

at Generating Facilities and to the subsequent connection of Large Loads Co-Located at

Generating Facilities under such tariffs.



Motion to Intervene and Comments

Federal Tariffs for Large Loads Co-Located at Generating Facilities 2
              A. Initial Position and Interests

        With respect to Federal interconnection tariffs for large loads co-located at generating

facilities: ALL reasonable costs and benefits must be properly weighed and applied; ALL

citizens and legal entities must have equal access to the tariffs (for example, a municipality, tribe

or any other entity can declare itself a Large Load, establish Co-Located Generation, and use any

federal tariff or a federally-regulated entity’s interconnection tariffs for Large Loads with Co-

Located Generation); no state law or policy can be subverted by any federal tariff or a federally-

regulated entity’s interconnection tariffs for Large Loads with Co-Located Generation); any

federal tariff or a federally-regulated entity’s interconnection tariffs for Large Loads with Co-

Located Generation) that directly results in public harm during grid emergencies and/or other

public emergencies is unjust and unreasonable. Finally, given the future expenses to be borne by

each and every state in this union, any federal tariff or federally-regulated entity’s

interconnection tariffs for Large Loads with Co-Located Generation) that subverts that State’s

ability to manage those expenses violates The Constitution of the United States of America.

        For the reasons set forth above, I have a direct and substantial interest which may be

materially affected by the outcome of this proceeding, and no other party is willing to represent

my interests. These interests are further shared by the public at large. As such, I respectfully

move to intervene.




Motion to Intervene and Comments

Federal Tariffs for Large Loads Co-Located at Generating Facilities 3

                                       II.      COMMENTS

                 Any and all tariffs approved by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission

(FERC) and/or approved by an entity regulated by FERC to interconnect large loads co-located

at generating facilities must meet the following requirements to preclude violating the Natural

Gas Act and The Constitution of the United States of America:

             1. The comprehensive economic public benefit of any Large Load and any Co-

                 Located Generating Facility subject to any such tariff must be established and

                 considered and demonstrated to mutually benefit ALL ratepayers, regardless of

                 any other tariff terms and conditions.

             2. Any Large-Load Customer and Co-Located Generating Facility must have open

                 and free access to any such tariff.

             3. States and Indigenous Tribes or Nations must have the ability to approve or reject

                 any terms of any interconnection under any such tariff.

             4. Any such tariff must include demand response conditions that preclude the Large

                 Load and/or Co-Located Generating Facility from having ANY impact on

                 congested grids during peak demand or public emergency response.




Motion to Intervene and Comments

Federal Tariffs for Large Loads Co-Located at Generating Facilities 4
